data.gender_notes: Curt is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from German Kurat, meaning 'guardian'. The Old English form, Cieret, means 'keeper' or 'ruler'. The name Curtis comes from the Latin word cor, meaning 'heart'. In Christianity, the name Curt is associated with St. Curatus, a Roman martyr. The name Curt carries the meaning “Brave, Courageous” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Curt usually hope their child will grow to embody brave, courageous and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Curt, derived from several ancient languages, has a long history in European culture. It suggests strength, protection, and rule, which may have appealed to parents looking for a strong and protective name for their child in the past. Historically, the name was probably most commonly used in Germanic-speaking regions, but it has been adopted in many other countries as well.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Curt is rooted in its meaning as a guardian or keeper. In Christian tradition, it is associated with St. Curatus, a Roman martyr who was carried off as a prisoner by pirates and, when they were unable to sell him, released him. According to legend, St. Curatus went on to live as a hermit, dedicating the rest of his life to prayer and penance. The name Curt, then, carries the meaning of a protector or guardian, reminding us of the importance of caring for others and for our own spiritual well-being. It is a reminder of the role we each play in guarding and protecting those around us, and of the need to be mindful of the spiritual needs of our own hearts and the hearts of those we encounter in our lives.
